method: Complete reads of eight pinned files with Git blob and SHA256 validation. No upstream suite execution.
findings: Basename, parent-directory, extension and stem tests explicitly exclude equal-content files based on optional name policies. These policies cannot be silently applied to exhaustive content equality. Most checks assert footer counts rather than complete path partitions.

Basename split test checks two groups of five equal-content files but does not assert their actual member paths. Relative-path combined-basename test additionally asserts the exact non-original path set.
Relative-path tests reject different directory depth and different basename; case-insensitive matching explicitly folds ASCII but does not fold the tested Cyrillic/umlaut names.
Extensionless regression distinguishes abc from abcd while accepting equal abc names in different directories. Extension tests do not cover dotfiles or multiple-dot suffix selection in these files.

test_pass_files.py:test_stdin_read actually passes direct path arguments to run_rmlint, not stdin. It checks two leading records and reclaimable-size footer but not full record count. It therefore must not be credited as another stdin transport test.

Empty-file lint test checks one zero-sized record but does not assert its path or type. Empty-directory simple case checks two types and sizes; deep case indexes expected suffixes without asserting total count. Hidden-file case confirms that ignored hidden children do not cause the parent to be reported empty.

Empty-file lint is distinct from duplicate-content grouping: its footer reports zero duplicates and zero reclaimable bytes. Our exact API treats equal empty files as a content partition, as separately validated by existing local tests.
limits: No production changes or new runtime coverage in this audit.
No complete rmlint or 500-repository review claim; native pHash/ASAN investigation remains skipped.
